name: Executive order of October 23, 1890 extinguishing Indian title to unallotted Ponca lands in Nebraska
nations: Ponca Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma
promises: The Indian Claims Commission records that the Acts of April 30, 1888 and March 2, 1889 confirmed reservation title in the Poncas of Nebraska and provided for allotments to them, after which the President was to declare Indian title extinguished to land not allotted.
Royce records that the order reserved from entry the tract occupied by the agency and school buildings of the old Ponca reservation (part of his area 472).
compensation: The Commission held in 1966 that the 27,235.90 acres on the former Ponca reservation in Nebraska confirmed to the tribe and allotted were partial, delayed compensation for the uncompensated loss of the reservation through the Sioux treaty of 1868. In Docket 323 it later awarded the Ponca just compensation for the 96,000 acre Nebraska reservation as of March 16, 1877, the date of removal: $1,004,589.49 with principal and interest to June 30, 1972.
today: The Commission's finding of a taking concerns the 1868 to 1877 loss of the same reservation (Royce area 472), which belongs to the Ponca treaty record; this 1890 order itself was not found to be a breach.

openQuestions: The 1877 taking of Royce area 472 found by the Commission in Docket 323 should be recorded on the Ponca treaty record that covers area 472 (kappler-883); it was kept out of this record because the 1890 order is a different event.
The Ponca Tribe of Nebraska's own account of the 1890 order was not located.
Audit 2026-11-08: the 1888 act date corrected from April 13 to April 30, 1888 (25 Stat. 94), per the Commission, Docket 323, 17 Ind. Cl. Comm. 162.

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for Ponca and Poncas (Court of Claims index) and 'Ponca 1890' (ICC); only Docket 323 and its Court of Claims appeals (183 Ct. Cl. 673; 197 Ct. Cl. 1065), which concern the earlier loss of the reservation; nothing on the 1890 order.
